content:
The three-digit all-identical numbers are \(111k\) for \(k=1,\dots,9\). We need
\[
\frac{n(n+1)}2=111k \quad\Rightarrow\quad n(n+1)=222k.
\]
Checking \(k=1,\dots,9\), only \(k=6\) gives a perfect square discriminant:
\[
\frac{n(n+1)}2=666 \quad\Rightarrow\quad n(n+1)=1332=36\cdot 37.
\]
Thus \(n=36\).

\[
\boxed{36}
\]
